LC Amendment Desk

Reads a supplier’s marked-up draft letter of credit — Word comments and tracked changes, PDF drafts, or remarks sent by email — and lays each requested change out in a seven-column amendment table for review.

Prototype, not published as an app. The screenshot uses a synthetic sample draft.

Type
Prototype · runs in the browser
Status
Prototype
Year
2026
Technologies
  • HTML
  • CSS
  • JavaScript
  • pdf.js

The problem

Supplier comments on a draft LC arrive in different forms. Each remark has to be matched to the right MT700 field, with the current wording beside the requested change, before the amendment request can be reviewed.

What it does

  • Extracts comments, tracked changes and highlights from a Word draft and matches each to its MT700 field, with the current wording beside the requested change.
  • Reads marked-up PDF drafts through pdf.js.
  • Splits remarks pasted from an email, drops greetings and sign-offs, and matches each remark to a field by tag, quoted wording or field name.
  • Leaves unclear remarks flagged as needing clarification instead of guessing.
  • Splits one comment that contains two separate requests into two amendment rows.
  • Editable review grid with search and sorting; export to Excel and Word.
